name: Nicodemus
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: the same came to Jesus by night. Why by night? It was a secret; he was a secret follower. But he believed on Christ.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, comes by night. Those men were the teachers of the synagogues, and it would have cost him standing to come openly.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

points: “There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews”: a man of position.
“Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.” They don’t talk much about his education, but to be a ruler he had position, a seat, like the bourgeois.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: Nicodemus takes it literally and asks whether a man can enter the second time into his mother's womb.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

points: “How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?” Nicodemus said, what are you talking about, being born again? You are going to climb back into your mother’s womb when you are already grown? Nicodemus had no idea what Christ was talking about.

source.name: TIPNR, Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References, by Tyndale House Cambridge, STEPBible.org

cases.name: Nicodemus
cases.charge: Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?; and bringing a hundred pound weight of myrrh and aloes
cases.preview: A Pharisee and ruler of the Jews came to Christ by night, acknowledged that his works showed God was with him, and was told that a man must be born again to see the kingdom of God (John 3:1-3).
